topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Reference Locality
explanation: Modern computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to bridge the performance gap between fast, expensive CPU registers and slower, cheaper main memory.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of storage with varying speeds and capacities. Caching strategies aim to exploit locality of reference (temporal and spatial) to improve performance by keeping frequently accessed data in faster levels of the hierarchy. This reduces the number of expensive main memory accesses.
